hook.line: Altamira keeps sending letters, and Tomás has had enough. Sometimes the most useful thing you can say is that something doesn't matter to you at all.
hook.es: Me importa un comino lo que diga Altamira.
hook.en: I couldn't care less what Altamira says.

examples.es: Me importa un comino lo que diga Altamira.
examples.en: I couldn't care less what Altamira says.

examples.es: A Hernando le importa un comino el fútbol.
examples.en: Hernando couldn't care less about soccer.

examples.es: ¿Te importa un comino lo que piensen?
examples.en: Do you not care one bit what they think? (to a friend)

examples.es: A ellos les importa un pito el ruido.
examples.en: They couldn't care less about the noise.

examples.es: Me importa un comino que Vale llegue tarde.
examples.en: I couldn't care less that Vale is late.

rule:
*Importar* works like *gustar*: the thing matters *to* someone, so you say *me importa*, *le importa*, *les importa*, and the thing comes after.
Add *un comino* (a cumin seed, something worthless) and it means "I couldn't care less". The meaning is already negative, so you don't need *no*: *Me importa un comino.* You can also say *un pepino* or *un pito*.
It is for friends and gossip, not for formal letters. *Me importa mucho* says the opposite: it matters a lot.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a negative-polarity idiom: a tiny, worthless thing stands in for "not at all".

readAndPick.es: Me importa un comino lo que diga Altamira.
options: Altamira's opinion matters a lot to me.
I couldn't care less what Altamira says.

readAndPick.es: Me importa mucho lo que piensas.
options: It matters a lot to me what you think.
I couldn't care less what you think.

readAndPick.es: A Hernando le importa un comino el fútbol.
options: Hernando loves soccer.
I couldn't care less about Hernando's soccer.
Hernando couldn't care less about soccer.
I don't care one bit.
It matters to me.
I'm not sure it matters to me.

readAndPick.es: Nos importa un comino la plata.
options: Money matters a lot to us.
Money doesn't matter to us at all.
Money doesn't matter to me at all.

readAndPick.es: ¿Te importa un comino lo que piensen?
options: Do they not care one bit what you think? (to a friend)
Do you not care one bit what they think? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: A mi hermana le importa un comino la moda.
options: My sister couldn't care less about fashion.
My sister loves fashion.

readAndPick.es: A ellos les importa un pito el ruido.
options: The noise doesn't bother me.
They are bothered by the noise.
They couldn't care less about the noise.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *me* or *le*, then type the whole sentence: ___ importa un comino lo que diga Altamira. (I couldn't care less what Altamira says.)
yourTurn.answer: Me importa un comino lo que diga Altamira.
yourTurn.why: The person who doesn't care is *me* here, so *me importa*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *le* or *les*, then type the whole sentence: A Hernando ___ importa un comino el fútbol. (Hernando couldn't care less about soccer.)
yourTurn.answer: A Hernando le importa un comino el fútbol.
accept: Le importa un comino el fútbol a Hernando.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I couldn't care less.
yourTurn.why: *Importar* plus *un comino* is the whole idiom.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: We couldn't care less about the noise.
yourTurn.answer: Nos importa un comino el ruido.
accept: Nos importa un pito el ruido.
Nos importa un pepino el ruido.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: They couldn't care less what Altamira says.
yourTurn.answer: Les importa un comino lo que diga Altamira.
accept: A ellos les importa un comino lo que diga Altamira.
Les importa un pito lo que diga Altamira.
yourTurn.why: *They* is *les*, and *lo que diga* follows the thing they don't care about.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it the opposite: *Me importa un comino la política.* becomes: Politics matters a lot to me.
yourTurn.why: *Mucho* replaces *un comino* when something does matter.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question to a friend: *Me importa un comino el ruido.* becomes: Do you not care one bit about the noise? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Asking a friend about themselves, the small word is *te*.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo importo un comino lo que diga.
pitfalls.right: Me importa un comino lo que diga.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Importar* works like *gustar*: the thing matters *to* you, so the small word is *me*.

pitfalls.wrong: A Hernando me importa un comino el fútbol.
pitfalls.right: A Hernando le importa un comino el fútbol.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The small word has to match the person who doesn't care: Hernando is *le*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me importa una comino la plata.
pitfalls.right: Me importa un comino la plata.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Comino* is masculine, so it is *un comino*.

personal: Tell me one thing you couldn't care less about. Say it with *me importa un comino*.
